decisions.reason: As a core rye bread presented on its own page in a growing market, it fits the firm's established capabilities and the visible launch commitment makes management inclined to continue it absent clear failure.
The premium raisin Christmas stollen has explicit public recognition with a gold medal, so dropping it would contradict a successful and visible commitment to a flagship seasonal product.

This seeded rye mixed bread is close to the existing assortment and has already been publicly introduced, so management can justify keeping it while treating any weak sales as temporary assortment adjustment.

Although somewhat more niche, the dark barley malt rye bread still builds directly on the bakery's bread expertise and prior public introduction, which under escalation of commitment favors retaining it for longer.
The marzipan Christmas stollen is a natural extension of the firm's confectionery and seasonal business, and the low development risk plus visible offering make withdrawal less likely within a year.

The ancient grain bread was promoted as the firm's newest 'Meisterstück,' signalling public commitment and identity value, so management is likely to persist with it unless results become unmistakably poor.
